_note: Cron in UTC. All tasks run in Review mode (agent proposes, humans approve). Keep cadence modest: every run consumes Azure Agent Units against the monthly cap.

scheduledTasks.name: w2-security-drift-daily
scheduledTasks.description: W2: daily security baseline drift and exposure triage (weekdays).
scheduledTasks.prompt: Since the previous run (or the last 24 hours), list in-scope landing zones with new high-severity unhealthy Defender for Cloud assessments, new public network access on PaaS resources in corp archetypes, policy noncompliance on security initiatives, and new Owner, Contributor or User Access Administrator assignments at subscription scope. Classify each finding (exposure, drift, identity, hardening), map it to the SE code and baseline rule, and name the owner. Do not change access or create exemptions.

scheduledTasks.name: w4-out-of-band-changes-daily
scheduledTasks.prompt: List changes in the platform subscriptions in the last 24 hours (Resource Graph resourcechanges) that were not made by a pipeline or deployment identity, for example portal or CLI changes by users. For each, give resource, change type, actor, time (DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM UTC) and the IaC module to reconcile. Summarize the count compared with the previous run.

scheduledTasks.name: w1-reliability-review-weekly
scheduledTasks.description: W1: weekly reliability and recovery-readiness review.
scheduledTasks.prompt: For the subscriptions in scope, list shared platform resources whose zone or instance configuration does not meet the tier matrix for their reliability-tier tag (or report configuration and missing targets if no tag exists). Add open HighAvailability Advisor recommendations, unhealthy Resource Health states and landing zones without a restore test in the required interval. For each gap state failure mode, evidence, owner and IaC change. Do not modify resources.

scheduledTasks.name: w3-cost-waste-weekly
scheduledTasks.description: W3 + UC11: weekly cost anomaly, waste and ingestion review.
scheduledTasks.prompt: Review the last 7 days compared with the previous 14 days: explain any cost or Log Analytics ingestion deviations by driver. List orphaned resources, subscriptions without a budget, and open Advisor Cost recommendations with estimated monthly savings in EUR, removal risk and owner. Include the SRE Agent's own Azure Agent Unit consumption. Do not delete or resize anything.

scheduledTasks.name: w5-capacity-headroom-weekly
scheduledTasks.description: W5: weekly capacity, quota and address-space headroom.
scheduledTasks.prompt: For the in-scope subscriptions and regions, report vCPU and AI model quota usage, subnet address usage in hub and spoke networks, and AKS scheduling or scale failures in the last 7 days. For each limit give usage, threshold, trend, projected exhaustion date and owner. Classify throttling as quota, capacity, configuration or demand. Do not request quota changes.

scheduledTasks.name: uc05-monitoring-blind-spots-weekly
scheduledTasks.description: UC05 + UC02: weekly monitoring blind spots and vended-subscription readiness.
scheduledTasks.prompt: List platform and landing-zone resources without diagnostic settings, without baseline (AMBA) alert rules, alert rules without action groups, and expected Log Analytics tables without data in the last 24 hours. Then delegate to the vending-governance subagent to list vended subscriptions missing mandatory tags, budgets or Defender plans, or with policy drift. Give owner and IaC fix per item.

scheduledTasks.name: uc10-backup-assurance-weekly
scheduledTasks.description: UC10: weekly backup and restore assurance.
scheduledTasks.prompt: List in-scope resources without backup protection where their tier requires it, failed or missing backup jobs in the last 7 days, vaults without soft delete or immutability, and landing zones without restore-test evidence in the required interval. Give owner and next action. Do not trigger backups or restores.

scheduledTasks.name: uc12-incident-to-waf-monthly
scheduledTasks.prompt: Review incidents, fired platform alerts and agent findings from the previous month. Group recurring issues, map each to the WAF pillar and checklist code it violated, the platform control that should have prevented it, and propose a reusable standard or IaC change for the CCoE backlog with owner. Include a one-line trend per WAF pillar.
